title: Settings, routers and typed request and response models
request: server.py holds most routes as closures and reads the environment in many places. Introduce one settings object read once, split the routes into routers per area that receive their dependencies through FastAPI Depends, and give every route pydantic request and response models, keeping every path, status code and payload as it is.
spec: dclab_rnd/settings.py (pydantic-settings); routers per area; pydantic models for every request and response; the frontend and tests need no changes. Done when server.py only builds the app, the OpenAPI schema describes every route, and a bad request body is a 422 everywhere.
plan: Check which tests depend on exact error text and when the tests set the model key, so reading settings once per app is safe.
Write settings.py; read empty variables as unset.

Move the routes into routers (core, research runs, projects, intern and lessons; the drafts in draft/api.py; each page in agentic/pages) that take the stores, the gateway and the running jobs through Depends(services).
Write request and response models that document and never trim (extra fields allowed, exclude_unset).
Reduce server.py to building the app; write test_api_contract (server only builds the app, every route has a model, a bad body is a 422).
Run the suite, the gate and the reviewer; fix; commit.

decisions.decision: Response models document and never trim: extra='allow' and exclude_unset.
decisions.why: The package promises unchanged payloads; a model that drops or adds keys would silently change what the frontend receives.

decisions.decision: A bad value of a mirrored setting (port, workspace budget) falls back to its default instead of stopping the server.
decisions.why: Those values were only read lazily before; failing at import would break make notebook, /mcp and every test over a setting nothing reads at start.

decisions.decision: A JSON body sent without a JSON content type is still read as JSON (uploads excepted).
decisions.why: The old routes always parsed the body whatever its type, and curl -d sends a form type; refusing it would change behaviour for existing clients.

decisions.decision: The model tiers and the database URL stay read by models.settings and storage.db.
decisions.why: They are read per request (keys, routing) and by command-line tools that build no app; moving them was not needed for the package and is listed as open.

change: New dclab_rnd/settings.py, agentic/services.py and api_models.py (a shared Router and typed models), routers in agentic/routers/ and draft/api.py and agentic/pages, all through Depends(services); server.py builds the app only; api_routes(app) walks included routers for the Platform page and the tests; tests/test_api_contract.py. The Platform test now checks the upload limit the route enforces instead of grepping server.py.

findings.defect: Strict settings parsing failed on empty variables.
findings.scenario: Tests set DCLAB_NO_LIVE_MODELS to an empty string; a strict boolean field refused '' and the app would not build.
findings.cause: pydantic-settings parses an empty string as a value.
findings.fix: Empty values are read as unset.
findings.test: The whole suite passes with the tests' empty variables.

findings.defect: After the split the Platform page would have listed no REST routes.
findings.scenario: The page walked app.routes for APIRoute entries; this FastAPI keeps an included router as one _IncludedRouter entry, so the lookup found none (the route-type count was 10 included routers, 4 routes, 2 mounts).
findings.cause: Included routers are not flattened into app.routes in this FastAPI version.
findings.fix: One helper, api_routes(app), walks included routers; the Platform page and the contract test use it.
findings.test: test_api_contract and the Platform page tests.

findings.defect: Two routes declared a dict response model but returned a list, so their normal path became a 500.
findings.scenario: GET /api/knowledge on a fresh app returned 500 (it returned [] before); POST /api/connectors/kaggle/search with a search that finds one dataset returned 500. No test called a successful search.
findings.cause: response_model=Page on routes whose functions return lists.
findings.test: PayloadTests.test_no_get_route_fails_on_real_ids calls every GET route with a real project, draft, session and record id and fails on any 5xx; PayloadTests.test_a_kaggle_search_returns_its_list.

findings.defect: exclude_unset was never applied, so responses gained new null keys.
findings.scenario: Each /api/projects item gained records, activity, graph, transitions and memory as null (the list was meant to be light); a started intern session gained trace: null; drafts gained solution: null. The frontend tolerated it, so nothing failed visibly.
findings.cause: Router.add_api_route used kwargs.setdefault, but FastAPI's api_route always passes response_model_exclude_unset=False explicitly, so the default never took effect (0 of 90 routes).

findings.defect: Unused settings could stop the server from importing, and an unprefixed environment variable changed one upload limit.
findings.scenario: DCLAB_PORT=abc or DCLAB_WORKSPACE_MONTHLY_EUR=5eur made importing the server fail (it builds the app at import), breaking make notebook, /mcp and every test; UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES=5 changed only the project upload route's limit while the draft route and the 413 message kept 200 MB.
findings.cause: Mirrored fields validated strictly at create_app, and upload_max_bytes had no DCLAB_ alias.
findings.fix: Port and workspace budget fall back to their defaults on a bad value; the upload limit is a constant on Services, not read from the environment.
findings.test: Re-checked with the bad values: the app builds with port 8765 and no cap.

findings.defect: A JSON body without a JSON content type was refused or silently ignored.
findings.scenario: POST /api/projects/{id}/approvals with a JSON body and no or text/plain content type gave 422 (it was parsed before); DELETE on a memory note received raw bytes, so the reason was dropped and the route answered 200.
findings.cause: FastAPI parses a body as JSON only when the content type says so; the old routes called request.json() regardless.
findings.fix: A middleware treats a missing, text/plain or form content type on /api/ writes as JSON (raw uploads ending in /data excepted); the memory route also loads a bytes body.

outcome: Done after one review round: one settings object per app, routers per area through Depends(services), typed models on every route, 87 operations in the OpenAPI schema, a non-JSON body a 422 everywhere; paths, status codes and payloads unchanged (610 tests on both stores and the four end-to-end flows pass).
lessons: A promise of 'payloads unchanged' needs a test that compares keys; the existing suite passed with every response carrying new nulls.
Check that a framework default you rely on is not overridden by an explicit argument further down (setdefault lost to an explicit False).
Call every GET route with real ids after a large refactor; a sweep finds response-model errors that unit tests miss.
Settings nothing reads at start must not be able to stop the server.
